question.text: Potassium dichromate when heated with concentrated sulphuric acid and a soluble chloride, gives brown-red vapours of :

solution.text:
Solid potassium dichromate when heated with concentrated sulphuric acid and a soluble chloride gives orange red vapours of a volatile oily liquid $\mathrm{CrO}_2 \mathrm{Cl}_2$
$\mathrm{K}_2 \mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7+4 \mathrm{NaCl}+6 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4\longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{KHSO}_4+4 \mathrm{NaHSO}_4+2 \mathrm{CrO}_2 \mathrm{Cl}_2$ chromyl chloride
